newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's BHP tumbles again as investors run.
newsitem.headline: Australia's BHP tumbles again as investors run.

text.p: Australia's largest company, the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, on Thursday saw its shares hit a two-year low after a sustained sell-off this week which has wiped more than A$2.25 billion (US$1.8 billion) off their market value.
The Australian miner, the world's biggest producer of copper, is being battered on the Australian stock market as copper prices continue to tumble, analysts said on Thursday.
BHP's share price breached a previous 1996 low of A$15.90, when it touched A$15.75 in afternoon trade, down 37 Australian cents, or 2.3 percent, to it lowest level since May 1994.
BHP shares have fallen nearly seven percent since Monday's open. The steel and resource giant represents about 10 percent of the Australian share market.
On Thursday morning brokers suggested the sell-off was overdone. "I think it's good value at these prices. It's probably a good buying opportunity," a Melbourne broker said.
However, resource analysts said on Thursday that BHP shares could go as low as A$15.0 or a five percent fall.
"I think the absolute downside would be A$15 and then people would just declare that it is ridiculously cheap," said Keith Williams a resource analyst at brokers BT Securities.

But copper prices continued to fall. In active trading in Sydney on Thursday the benchmark three-month contract was quoted at US$1,862.00-$1,872.00 a tonne, well down on Wednesday's LME afternoon kerb close of $1,915.

BHP, which reported a 14 percent slump in group net profit after abnormals in the year to May 31, is due to release its August quarter results on September 20 amid recent earnings downgrades for 1996/97 profit from some major brokerages.
